**Written Statement Regarding October 27 Afternoon Route**  
**Bus 41, Route 9 Elementary**

Dear Mrs. Okafor,

I am writing in response to your complaint dated October 29 concerning the afternoon bus route on Tuesday, October 27. Darlene gave me a copy of the complaint on November 3 and asked me to provide a written statement for the transportation office. I understand that you will receive a copy as well, so I want to explain what happened from my perspective.

First, I understand how frightening it must have been not to see Amara get off the bus as expected. I have grandchildren, and I would have been worried too. I am sorry that you and Amara had a difficult afternoon. I also want you to know that my decision to return her to school was made because I could not see an adult at the stop and was following the district’s rule for kindergarten riders.

On October 27, I was driving Bus 41 on the Route 9 elementary afternoon run. Amara, a kindergarten student at Fairmont Elementary, had a green tag on her bag. That tag indicates that an adult must be present at the stop before she can be released from the bus.

I arrived at the Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street stop at approximately 3:52 p.m. The scheduled time was 3:50 p.m. I waited until approximately 3:55 p.m., but I did not see an adult at the corner. Under the district rule for kindergarten riders, when no adult is at the stop, the student remains on the bus and is returned to school, where the office contacts the parent. Because I could not see an adult, I kept Amara on the bus and continued the route.

At approximately 3:56 p.m., I radioed dispatch. Gloria at dispatch called the school. At that point, I still had three stops to complete and 14 children on the bus. I could not leave the bus and the children unattended to go across the road to look for an adult.

I understand from your complaint that you were parked across Brandt Street near the laundromat and waved to me. I did not see you or see anyone wave. There was a box truck parked on that side of the street. I do not doubt that you were concerned and trying to get my attention; I can only say that I did not see you from the bus.

I also understand that you reported seeing me drive off laughing. I was not laughing. As I pulled away, I was telling a fourth-grade student in seat 2 to sit back down. I wanted that student seated while the bus was moving.

Amara remained on the bus while I completed the remaining stops. She appeared fine to me and was coloring on her folder. She asked if she could ride more, and I told her we were going on a little extra trip. I returned her to Fairmont Elementary at approximately 4:31 p.m. and personally walked her into the office and left her with Mrs. Petrakis.

I have driven a school bus for 28 years and have had no write-ups. My responsibility is to get the children on my bus where they need to go safely and to follow the district’s procedures. Returning Amara to school was not a decision I made lightly, and it was not intended to cause you worry. Based on what I could see at the stop, I followed the rule that applies when an adult is not present for a kindergarten rider.

I respectfully ask the transportation office to **preserve and review the Bus 41 camera footage** from the afternoon of October 27, including the footage from the Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street stop and as the bus pulled away. I believe it is important to review the available footage as part of the complaint.

Mrs. Okafor, I would like us to avoid another situation like this. Going forward, would you please stand on the bus side of the street or step out of your car where I can see you when the bus arrives? I understand that things can happen, but being able to see you at the stop will help me know that Amara can be safely released.

I am glad to continue driving Amara, and I want to resolve this respectfully. Thank you for taking the time to read my account.

Sincerely,

[Driver’s Name]  
Bus Driver, Bus 41  
[Date]
